findings.title: Corroborated anomaly: monthly income on application_form.pdf ('95,000.00')
findings.explanation:
3 findings from independent methods point at the same value. Visual/file forensics show signs of alteration AND contextual logic shows the value does not fit the rest of the evidence. Either kind of signal alone could be noise; together they make deliberate alteration the most likely explanation. This is not a fraud determination: human verification with the issuing source is required.
- [F-001] Overwritten value: '58,000.00' hidden under '95,000.00' (visual, deterministic, confidence 0.95)
- [F-004] Declared income exceeds payslip earnings (cross_document, deterministic, confidence 0.90)
- [F-007] Font inconsistency in 'monthly_income' (visual, deterministic, confidence 0.85)
findings.recommendation: Escalate for manual review; verify the value with the issuing source.

findings.title: Overwritten value: '58,000.00' hidden under '95,000.00'
findings.explanation: The PDF text layer contains the value '58,000.00' (font Helvetica) at the same position as the displayed value '95,000.00' (font Times-Roman). The displayed value was drawn later, on top of the original. Legitimate document generators do not produce overlapping values, so this is strong evidence that the field was altered after the document was created.
findings.recommendation: Treat the displayed value as unverified; obtain the original from the issuer.

findings.title: Signature appears to be a digital copy
findings.explanation: The applicant's signature on application_form.pdf and the signature on identity_card.jpg are near-identical in shape (correlation 0.97). Two genuine hand signatures always vary slightly in stroke path and proportions; a match this close is characteristic of one signature image being copied and pasted onto the other document.
findings.recommendation: Obtain a wet-ink signature in the presence of staff.

findings.title: Salary credited differs from payslip net pay
findings.explanation: The bank statement shows a salary credit of 49,500.00 ('SALARY CREDIT KESTREL'), but the salary slip for the same period states a net pay of 94,500.00 (difference 45,000.00). The bank credit is produced independently of the payslip, so one of the two documents does not reflect the actual salary.
findings.recommendation: Ask the employer to confirm the salary paid.

findings.title: Declared income exceeds payslip earnings
findings.explanation: The application declares a monthly income of 95,000.00, which is 64% higher than the gross earnings of 58,000.00 on the salary slip submitted as proof (net pay printed: 94,500.00).
findings.recommendation: Verify income with employer / tax records.

findings.title: Net pay does not equal gross minus deductions
findings.explanation: Gross 58,000.00 - Deductions 8,500.00 = 49,500.00, but the slip shows Net Pay 94,500.00 (difference 45,000.00). Because the earnings and deduction components are internally consistent, the Net Pay figure is the one that does not fit.
findings.recommendation: Obtain payroll confirmation from the employer.

findings.title: Noise-free patch in scanned document (over net_pay)
findings.explanation: The rest of the page has uniform scanner noise (median residual 3.3); this 3-block region has only 0% of that noise. A smooth patch like this is typical of content painted or pasted digitally after scanning (e.g. a white box used to cover a value).

evidence.note: value lies on/near the noise-free patch

findings.recommendation: Compare against an independently sourced copy.

findings.title: Font inconsistency in 'monthly_income'
findings.explanation: This value is typeset differently from every other value on the form: font 'Times-Roman' is used only 1x in the document (others: Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold); font size 10.5pt vs 10.0pt for other values. A document produced by one generator normally uses one font for all values.

evidence.note: font 'Times-Roman' is used only 1x in the document (others: Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold); font size 10.5pt vs 10.0pt for other values

findings.title: Typography/alignment irregularity in 'net_pay'
findings.explanation: Printed forms place every value on the same baseline and in the same font. This value deviates: baseline offset +4px relative to its label (typical -0px); text height 115% of comparable values. Such deviations commonly appear when a value is retyped or pasted over the original, but can also result from scanning skew or OCR box noise.

evidence.note: baseline offset +4px relative to its label (typical -0px); text height 115% of comparable values

findings.title: Creator and producer software differ
findings.explanation: Created by 'Synthetic DocGen 1.0' but last written by 'QuickPDF Editor 7.2'. The producer is a PDF editing tool.

findings.title: PDF was modified after creation (1 revision(s))
findings.explanation: The file contains 2 end-of-file markers, meaning 1 incremental update(s) were appended after the original was written. Updates are normal for signing or form filling, but also how PDF editors save changes.

findings.title: Modification date differs from creation date
Elevated error level around '94,500.00'
findings.explanation: Error Level Analysis: this text recompresses 1.37x more strongly than typical body text on the page (robust z-score 4.0). Content inserted after the image was last compressed often behaves this way. ELA is weak when the whole file was re-saved at the same quality and is sensitive to contrast, so on its own this is only a pointer for review.
findings.recommendation: Inspect the original scan / request the source document.

limitations: OCR output is treated as unverified input; low-confidence reads are flagged in explanations.
Visual forensics are heuristic: ELA and noise analysis can be affected by re-scanning, heavy compression, photos of screens, and image resizing. A clean result does not prove authenticity.
Signature analysis detects absence and near-identical copies only; it cannot authenticate a signature.
Field extraction relies on printed labels; documents with unusual layouts may yield missing fields.
Only the first 5 pages of a PDF are analysed.
Thresholds were calibrated on the synthetic demonstration dataset; real-world documents need recalibration.
No finding is a fraud determination. Human review is required before any consequential decision.
